findings.statement: The provider requires post-create and refresh permissions beyond the obvious Terraform create mutations.

aws_s3_bucket is the dominant permission-expansion source because its legacy refresh path reads policy, ACL, CORS, website, versioning, acceleration, request payment, logging, lifecycle, replication, encryption, Object Lock and location.
IAM policy, IAM role, KMS key, KMS alias, Secrets Manager secret and CloudTrail resources all perform mandatory read-back or enumeration calls after create.
The provider auxiliary gap is no longer an unknown action-set gap; it is now primarily an exact runtime cardinality and environment-branch gap.
No AWS or Terraform execution is required to include the source-confirmed action set in the effective-permission gate.

gate_reconciliation.required_update: Merge all confirmed mutation and post-create/read actions into the exact action-resource-context matrix before executing the read-only gate.
gate_reconciliation.critical_resource_specific_rule: Model aws_s3_bucket legacy read actions for each of the three exact bucket ARNs even when dedicated resources own the configurations.
gate_reconciliation.pass_semantics: A gate PASS requires every source-confirmed action-resource-context pair to evaluate allowed, with no missing context, no explicit deny and no unresolved Organizations scope.

limitations: Static source review does not prove exact API call counts because retry loops and eventual-consistency waiters are runtime-dependent.
Source review cannot establish SCP or RCP applicability in the target AWS organization.
SimulatePrincipalPolicy cannot reproduce every service-internal validation or cross-service resource-policy behavior.
Conditional partition fallback calls are retained as fail-closed considerations but are not expected in the standard AWS partition used by the plan.
